chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmee, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The foundling is free; when he grows up, if he wishes, he may maintain the relationship with the one who picked him up, and if not, he shall return the maintenance to him and go his way, so he may maintain the relationship with whomever he wishes.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a foundling regarding maintenance and guardianship upon reaching adulthood?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the contractual nature of *ilqat* (adoption by finding), establishing that the foundling's freedom is inherent but the financial bond with the finder is conditional. It highlights the principle of *ikhtiyar* (choice) upon maturity, allowing the individual to either formalize the relationship through repayment of *nafaqah* (maintenance) or dissolve it, reflecting the flexibility of personal status law in the Imami tradition.
